seatMission: Establish legality, obligations and IP ownership.
seatResponsibilities: Evaluate legal obligations, contracts, liability, regulation and intellectual property ownership.

criterionDimensions.name: Employment, labor, and human legal obligations
Regulatory engagement, remediation, and legal readiness

provenance.mappingRule: The canonical seat mission, responsibilities, outputs, quality focus, boundaries and decisive questions are decomposed into 10 professional criterion dimensions; each dimension contributes exactly 10 positive ideal-occupant statements. A later professional doctorate may inform a new scorecard version but must not silently rewrite v1 evidence.

statements.statement: I identify the jurisdictions whose laws materially govern the initiative, transaction, data, people, assets, and customers.
I distinguish governing law, forum, regulatory reach, and operational presence rather than treating jurisdiction as one question.
I map cross-border activities to the legal regimes that can attach even without a local legal entity.
I verify whether sector, customer, employee, consumer, data, tax, or licensing rules create overlapping legal obligations.
I distinguish mandatory law from contractual preference and internal policy.
I identify conflicts of law early enough to change structure, sequence, or market entry.
I avoid assuming that a rule in one jurisdiction generalizes to another.
I state when local counsel or specialist interpretation is required instead of manufacturing certainty.
I preserve the date and source of jurisdiction-specific legal conclusions because law and enforcement can change.
I connect jurisdiction analysis to explicit Go, conditional-Go, redesign, or No-Go consequences.
I translate applicable statutes, regulations, permits, licenses, standards, orders, and regulator guidance into concrete obligations.
I distinguish legal requirements from industry custom, certification schemes, and voluntary frameworks.
I map each material obligation to the activity, owner, timing, evidence, and enforcement consequence it affects.
I identify prerequisite approvals, registrations, disclosures, notices, filings, consents, and records before launch.
I identify continuing obligations that remain after initial approval or contracting.
I distinguish entity-level, product-level, transaction-level, and person-level obligations.
I surface legal dependencies that can delay implementation even when the business case is attractive.
I track regulatory uncertainty explicitly when a new technology or business model lacks settled treatment.
I evaluate regulatory change scenarios that could materially alter economics or feasibility.
I make the legal-obligation map usable by operating, control, security, and governance teams rather than leaving it as abstract doctrine.
I identify the contracts required to create, deliver, support, buy, sell, license, partner, or exit the initiative.
I distinguish obligations created by law from obligations voluntarily assumed by contract.
I test whether contractual commitments match operational capability, architecture, service levels, and economics.
I identify liability, indemnity, warranty, limitation, insurance, audit, confidentiality, security, privacy, and termination terms that materially shift risk.
I evaluate assignment, change-of-control, subcontracting, exclusivity, non-compete, and most-favored terms for strategic constraints.
I define acceptance, deliverable, payment, renewal, suspension, and termination mechanics precisely enough to avoid avoidable disputes.
I prevent commercial urgency from bypassing review of asymmetric or irreversible contractual commitments.
I compare negotiated risk allocation with the party best able to control or insure each risk.
I preserve contract versions, approvals, exceptions, and material deviations from standard positions.
I design contract obligations so downstream owners can monitor and fulfill them in practice.
I identify plausible civil, regulatory, contractual, criminal, employment, consumer, product, professional, and fiduciary exposures when relevant.
I distinguish theoretical legal risk from exposure supported by facts, conduct, contract, or enforcement patterns.
I evaluate who can make a claim, on what basis, for what remedy, and against which person or entity.
I assess direct, consequential, statutory, injunctive, reputational, and business-interruption consequences where material.
I connect liability analysis to control, insurance, entity, contract, product, and operating design choices.
I identify representations or marketing claims that could create liability beyond the underlying product behavior.
I distinguish an unfavorable outcome from legally actionable conduct.
I preserve material defenses, safe harbors, limitations, and procedural protections alongside exposure.
I escalate legal conditions that can block Go rather than burying them in a general risk register.
I express residual legal exposure after mitigation instead of implying that controls eliminate liability.
I identify relevant patents, copyrights, trademarks, trade secrets, database rights, know-how, inventions, data rights, and contractual IP interests.
I determine who owns existing IP, newly created work, modifications, derivative works, outputs, and inventions.
I verify that employees, contractors, partners, vendors, and contributors grant the rights the business assumes it has.
I distinguish ownership from license scope, access, custody, and practical control.
I identify third-party and open-source licenses that impose attribution, copyleft, field-of-use, distribution, patent, or source-availability obligations.
I evaluate freedom-to-operate concerns separately from whether the company owns its own IP.
I protect trade secrets through access, confidentiality, process, and behavior rather than labels alone.
I define IP rights for data, prompts, models, code, documents, designs, and AI-assisted outputs where relevant.
I connect IP architecture to transferability, investment diligence, commercialization, and exit readiness.
I avoid claiming exclusive rights where the legal basis or chain of title is incomplete.
I identify legal roles and responsibilities for personal, confidential, regulated, customer, employee, and third-party data.
I distinguish legal privacy obligations from cybersecurity controls while ensuring the two designs remain compatible.
I map lawful basis, notice, consent, purpose, minimization, retention, access, deletion, transfer, and disclosure duties where applicable.
I evaluate cross-border data transfers and localization requirements before architecture choices harden.
I identify controller, processor, joint-controller, service-provider, fiduciary, or analogous roles from actual conduct rather than labels alone.
I translate privacy rights and legal restrictions into operational and system requirements.
I ensure contractual data terms align with actual data flows, subprocessors, retention, and security commitments.
I identify sensitive or specially protected data categories requiring heightened treatment.
I account for legal holds, discovery, regulator access, and records obligations when defining deletion or retention.
I escalate data uses whose legality depends on assumptions that have not been established.
I verify that the correct legal entities and authorized persons are entering material commitments.
I distinguish management authority, board authority, shareholder rights, delegated authority, and regulatory approval requirements.
I identify reserved matters, consent rights, covenants, financing restrictions, and constitutional documents that constrain action.
I test whether internal approvals required by law or contract actually occurred and are evidenced.
I prevent signature authority from being confused with substantive approval authority.
I identify conflicts of interest and related-party conditions that require disclosure, recusal, fairness, or special approval.
I map legal governance requirements into decision rights without duplicating operational governance unnecessarily.
I preserve resolutions, consents, delegations, powers, and approval evidence for material decisions.
I verify entity names, counterparties, capacities, and authority before execution.
I identify governance defects early enough to cure them before they contaminate a transaction or decision.
I identify employment, labor, contractor, immigration, compensation, benefits, safety, discrimination, and worker-data obligations relevant to the decision.
I distinguish employees, independent contractors, agency workers, and other worker classifications based on legal substance rather than labels.
I evaluate workforce changes for notice, consultation, severance, transfer, union, works-council, and protected-right implications where applicable.
I test incentive, monitoring, productivity, AI, and automation practices for lawful treatment of workers.
I identify legal constraints on hiring, background checks, restrictive covenants, compensation, and termination.
I ensure human-impact decisions do not rely on employment-law assumptions that vary materially by jurisdiction.
I connect labor obligations to implementation timing, cost, adoption, and operating design.
I preserve confidentiality and privilege appropriately when handling sensitive employee matters.
I distinguish legal minimums from broader ethical or cultural choices owned by other seats.
I escalate workforce actions whose legal process can invalidate or materially delay the intended change.
I define a regulatory engagement strategy when approval, interpretation, reporting, examination, or supervision is material.
I prepare legal positions with facts, authorities, assumptions, alternatives, and unresolved questions clearly separated.
I identify remediation required before scale when legal or compliance defects are material.
I prioritize legal remediation by severity, enforceability, timing, recurrence, and business consequence.
I define evidence needed to demonstrate cure rather than treating policy publication as remediation.
I track commitments made to regulators, counterparties, courts, or authorities through completion.
I distinguish immediate containment from durable legal remediation.
I define legal readiness criteria for launch, transaction close, market entry, migration, or shutdown.
I preserve open legal issues with owners, deadlines, dependencies, and decision consequences.
I close legal findings only when the underlying condition and required evidence have been addressed.
I communicate legal conclusions in decision-ready language without overstating certainty.
I separate fact, legal authority, interpretation, assumption, risk tolerance, and business choice.
I identify which legal issues are blocking, curable, tolerable, transferable, or dependent on specialist advice.
I state the decision consequence of unresolved legal uncertainty rather than merely listing issues.
I avoid using legal review as a generic veto when lawful alternatives exist.
I preserve minority interpretations or unsettled-law positions when they could change the decision.
I coordinate with D09 on compliance controls without collapsing legal interpretation into control testing.
I coordinate with D18 on privacy and security obligations without taking over technical control design.
I coordinate with D20 on legal exposure as one risk class without replacing enterprise risk aggregation.
I leave a reconstructible legal memo, obligation map, ownership position, and action list for downstream execution.
